messages.author: 050ef3ac9ac6ec03
messages.subject: Extracting information on model convergence
parts:
Dear all,


I am running a large number of INLA models, and have a large proportion that are not converging, which I want to look at in more detail. I have several general questions.


1. Is there any way to distinguish models that have converged from ones that have not, from the fit object after the models have run (the ‘large bru’ produced by the lgcp function)?


2. Is there a way to extract the convergence history from a fit object, i.e. the number of iterations run before convergence, and/or the maximum deviation from previous at each iteration? I know these are output to the console during the lgcp function, but I need to extract them afterwards if possible.


3. Is it possible to change the convergence criterion, i.e. from 1% max deviation from previous, to 2%?


Any advice on any of the queries would be much appreciated.


Many thanks in advance,

Charles

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Extracting information on model convergence
parts:
sorry for late reply. Not converging is usually a result of a flexible
with with not that informative data. Since the data are given, then,
its all about using informative priors and not asking to much of the
model.

to check that all went fine, you may use

> r=inla(...)
> r$ok
[1] TRUE


H

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Extracting information on model convergence
parts:
Yes, for inla() models that’s true, but for bru() models with nonlinear predictors there is the iterated inla convergence as well, and that’s what’s causing the issue in this case.

I just checked the inlabru code, and it does store the convergence information:
“result$iinla$track = do.call(rbind, track)”
If your final bru output object is called “fit”, take a look at
fit$iinla$track

It does however seem that the structure of that output isn’t in the most practical format possible; please open another issue on the inlabru github about it...

Finn

I've now got the model track data (from fit$iinla$track) with estimate information for each iteration.

I've tried a few things to try and get the Max deviation from previous that the 1% convergence criterion is based on, but I can't work out how to obtain it from the track data.

Any advice much appreciated.

Many thanks,

Charles
